description: Composite figure combining six SEM micrographs of near-rapidly solidified Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr steel strips with one engineering stress-strain plot. (a)-(c) are the as-cast 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr strips; (d)-(f) are the same alloys after annealing. Every micrograph carries a 20 µm scale bar and yellow arrows labelling the dark δ-ferrite phase and the lighter γ-austenite matrix. In (a) the δ-ferrite is small, sparse and short-rod shaped; it coarsens as Cr rises. In (b) skeletal/blocky δ appears, and in (c) the δ-ferrite is large, interconnected and blocky with an obviously higher area fraction. The annealed series (d)-(f) follows the same trend with more and coarser δ-ferrite, (f) 6Cr being the most heavily populated. The last panel is an engineering stress-strain plot (Engineering Stress 0-1200 MPa vs Engineering Strain 0-50%) with three curves labelled 0Cr (black), 3Cr (red) and 6Cr (blue); the 6Cr curve reaches the highest stress and the largest elongation. Together the panels link rising Cr content plus annealing to a larger δ-ferrite fraction and show the resulting tensile response.

observations.observation: All six micrographs carry a 20 µm scale bar and yellow arrows explicitly labelling 'δ' (dark phase) and 'γ' (matrix).
In the as-cast 0Cr micrograph (a) the δ-ferrite consists of small, sparse, short rod-shaped particles in the γ-austenite matrix.
In the as-cast 6Cr micrograph (c) the δ-ferrite is coarse, blocky and partially interconnected, at a visibly higher area fraction than in (a).
The annealed 6Cr micrograph (f) shows the highest apparent δ-ferrite density of the six panels, with interconnected blocky networks.
The stress-strain panel is plotted as Engineering Stress/MPa (0-1200) against Engineering Strain/% (0-50) with curves labelled 0Cr (black), 3Cr (red) and 6Cr (blue).
In the stress-strain plot the 6Cr (blue) curve reaches the highest stress and the largest elongation, while 3Cr (red) has the lowest curve.
The caption states the micrographs are of Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr steel strips, as-cast (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr and annealed (d) 0Cr, (e) 3Cr, (f) 6Cr.
The citing text states the volume fractions of δ-ferrite in the as-cast 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr strips are 3%, 12% and 18%, respectively.
The citing text states annealing at 600 °C for 3 h raises the δ-ferrite volume fraction to 6%, 14% and 24% for 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr, respectively.
The citing text states the irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite matrix and that Cr addition changes the short rod-shape ferrite into block ferrite.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of as-cast 0Cr strip; sparse, short rod-shaped dark δ-ferrite particles (yellow arrow 'δ') dispersed in a lighter γ-austenite matrix (yellow arrow 'γ'); 20 µm scale bar lower right.
SEM micrograph of as-cast 3Cr strip; δ-ferrite (yellow arrow 'δ') now skeletal/blocky, larger and more numerous than in (a); γ matrix arrowed; 20 µm scale bar.
SEM micrograph of as-cast 6Cr strip; coarse, blocky, partly interconnected δ-ferrite particles at clearly higher area fraction; γ matrix arrowed; 20 µm scale bar.
SEM micrograph of annealed 0Cr strip; small rod-like and branched δ-ferrite in γ matrix, similar size to (a) but with more branching; 20 µm scale bar.
SEM micrograph of annealed 3Cr strip; multiple blocky δ-ferrite particles distributed in the γ matrix; 20 µm scale bar.
SEM micrograph of annealed 6Cr strip; the most densely populated panel, with large interconnected blocky δ-ferrite networks in γ matrix; 20 µm scale bar.

Engineering stress-strain curves, x-axis Engineering Strain/% 0-50, y-axis Engineering Stress/MPa 0-1200; curves labelled 0Cr (black), 3Cr (red) and 6Cr (blue); 6Cr attains the highest stress and the largest strain at fracture.

unreadable_items: No δ-ferrite area-fraction values are printed on any micrograph; the 3/12/18% and 6/14/24% values exist only in the citing text
The stress-strain curves carry no printed numeric values beyond the axis ticks and curve labels, so peak stress and elongation cannot be read exactly
